### 📅 **Timeline Cards: Life and Legacy of John William Robert Kerr, 7th Marquess of Lothian**

---

#### **Card 1: Birth and Early Life (1794–1815)**  
**Date:** 1 February 1794  
- Born John William Robert Kerr.  
- Styled **Lord Newbottle** from birth (courtesy title of eldest son of the 6th Marquess).  
- Son of William Kerr, 6th Marquess of Lothian, and Lady Harriet (daughter of John Hobart, 2nd Earl of Buckinghamshire).  

**Transition:**  
- 1815: Upon his father’s succession to the marquessate, he is styled **Earl of Ancram** (a courtesy title) and begins to take on public roles.

---

#### **Card 2: Political and Military Appointments (1815–1824)**  
**Date:** 1815  
- Becomes **Earl of Ancram** upon his father’s succession to the Marquessate.  

**Date:** 1820  
- Enters the **House of Commons** as one of two representatives for **Huntingdon**.  
- Holds the seat until 1824.  

**Date:** 1824  
- Succeeds his father as **Colonel of the Edinburgh Militia**.  
- Succeeds his father as **Lord-Lieutenant of Roxburghshire**.  

---

#### **Card 3: Later Political and Honorary Roles (1824–1841)**  
**Date:** September 1841  
- Sworn of the **Privy Council** (PC).  
- Appointed **Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard** in Sir Robert Peel’s Tory government.  
- Holds the position until his death in November 1841.  

**Note:** This appointment was brief but significant, reflecting his standing in the government at the time of his death.

---

#### **Card 4: Marriage and Family (1831–1841)**  
**Date:** 1831  
- Marries **Lady Cecil Chetwynd-Talbot**, daughter of Charles Chetwynd-Talbot, 2nd Earl Talbot.  
- They have **five sons and two daughters**.  

**Key descendants:**  
- **William Kerr** and **Schomberg Kerr** – both succeeded to the marquessate.  
- **Lord Ralph Kerr** – became a **major-general**; father of **Philip Kerr, 11th Marquess of Lothian**.  
- **Lord Walter Kerr** – became an **admiral** in the Royal Navy;  
  - Grandfather of **Peter Kerr, 12th Marquess of Lothian**;  
  - Great-grandfather of **Michael Kerr, 13th Marquess of Lothian**.  

---

#### **Card 5: Death and Legacy (1841–1877)**  
**Date:** 14 November 1841  
- Dies at age 47.  
- Dies in office as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard and Lord-Lieutenant of Roxburghshire.  

**Posthumous Events:**  
- After his death, the **Marchioness of Lothian** (his wife) converts to **Catholicism** with her two younger sons, **Lord Ralph Kerr** and **Lord Walter Kerr**, and her daughters.  
- **Marchioness of Lothian** dies in **May 1877**, aged 69.  

---

### 🔍 Summary of Key Transitions (Chronological Flow)

| Year | Event |
|------|-------|
| 1794 | Born John William Robert Kerr; styled Lord Newbottle |
| 1815 | Becomes Earl of Ancram upon father’s succession to Marquessate |
| 1820 | Enters House of Commons for Huntingdon |
| 1824 | Succeeds father as Colonel of Edinburgh Militia and Lord-Lieutenant of Roxburghshire |
| 1831 | Marries Lady Cecil Chetwynd-Talbot |
| 1841 (Sept) | Sworn of Privy Council; appointed Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard |
| 1841 (Nov 14) | Dies at age 47; legacy continues through descendants

### 🔑 Key Figures List (Lothian Marquess Family – Generational Connections)

1. **John William Robert Kerr, 7th Marquess of Lothian (1794–1841)**  
   – Eldest son of William Kerr, 6th Marquess; styled Lord Newbottle until 1815, then Earl of Ancram.  
   – Entered Parliament for Huntingdon (1820–1824); served as Colonel of Edinburgh Militia and Lord-Lieutenant of Roxburghshire.  
   – Briefly served as Captain of the Yeomen of the Guard under Sir Robert Peel (1841).  
   – Married Lady Cecil Chetwynd-Talbot in 1831; father of five sons and two daughters.  
   – Died in 1841; pivotal figure in establishing the political and military legacy of the family.

2. **William Kerr, 8th Marquess of Lothian**  
   – Second son of John William Robert Kerr; succeeded his father in 1841.  
   – First in the line of successors to hold the marquessate after the 7th Marquess.  
   – Key figure in continuing the family’s political influence.

3. **Schomberg Kerr, 9th Marquess of Lothian**  
   – Third son of John William Robert Kerr; succeeded his brother William.  
   – Held the marquessate after William; part of the direct line of succession.  
   – Less prominent in public life, but essential in maintaining the title’s continuity.

4. **Lord Ralph Kerr (major-general)**  
   – Third son of John William Robert Kerr; became a **major-general in the army**.  
   – **Father of Philip Kerr, 11th Marquess of Lothian**.  
   – Key military figure; bridges the family into the 19th-century military elite.

5. **Lord Walter Kerr (admiral)**  
   – Fourth son of John William Robert Kerr; became an **admiral in the Royal Navy**.  
   – **Grandfather of Peter Kerr, 12th Marquess of Lothian**.  
   – **Great-grandfather of Michael Kerr, 13th Marquess of Lothian**.  
   – Critical link in the naval branch of the family’s legacy.

6. **Philip Kerr, 11th Marquess of Lothian**  
   – Son of Lord Ralph Kerr.  
   – Direct descendant of the 7th Marquess; continues the line of the marquessate.  
   – Noted for his role in British politics and diplomacy (later known for his work in the 20th century).

7. **Peter Kerr, 12th Marquess of Lothian**  
   – Grandson of Lord Walter Kerr.  
   – Successor to the marquessate after Philip Kerr.  
   – Maintains the family’s noble lineage through the naval branch.

8. **Michael Kerr, 13th Marquess of Lothian**  
   – Great-grandson of Lord Walter Kerr.  
   – Current holder of the title (as of the document’s context).  
   – Represents the continuation of the family’s legacy through the naval line.
